headline: PILOT DONE — StatusDot is drawn into the Figma staging copy (2VgBbVpKiDnu0aftJEVyBQ, page 'StatusDot', set 2003:21) by an agent, from the manifest, via the Figma MCP. 18 variants (6 tones x 3 sizes), named to the file's existing convention, fills bound to color/feedback/* and color/content/secondary, radius bound to radius/full, geometry deliberately left literal because the code sizes are raw Tailwind with no HDS token behind them (inventing statusDot/* variables would manufacture drift against ADR-025). Verified structurally (get_metadata) and visually (screenshot). The published library was never written to. Answer to the pilot question: the other 40 ARE mechanical, and the recipe is written down in figma/COMPONENT-DRAWING-RECIPE.md. THE REAL FIND: verifying the fills were genuinely variable-bound turned up that Figma's dark mode is entirely unwired — all 189 mode-aware variables (110 Semantic + 79 Component) are byte-identical in Light and Dark, while code ships a full [data-theme=dark] block (content.secondary neutral-600->neutral-400, feedback.success green-700->green-400). Filed #252. No component rework is implied: StatusDot binds to the right variables and will render dark correctly the moment the collections are fixed. Nothing caught it because check:figma-drift has never run against real state (#236). Walkthrough: docs/figma-statusdot-pilot-2026-09-21.html

blocked: ENVIRONMENT, mostly fixed 2026-09-21 — read this before re-diagnosing anything network-shaped. The cloud environment's network policy was set to Custom and api.figma.com + registry.npmjs.org were added. api.figma.com is now REACHABLE (it answers 401 rather than a gateway 403). registry.npmjs.org is still denied with an explicit 'x-deny-reason: host_not_allowed', because it sits in the container's noProxy set and therefore BYPASSES the agent proxy — the Custom domain list governs the proxied path, not the direct one. The fix is the 'Also include default list of common package managers' checkbox in the environment dialog. If pnpm install still 403s in a new session, that checkbox is the thing to check, not the allowlist

The Figma PAT in THIS session's container is genuinely dead — api.figma.com answers 401 now that it is reachable. Adrian rotated it into the environment on 2026-09-21, but env vars are baked at container boot, so only a NEW session picks the new key up. CORRECTION to earlier handoffs: the previous 403 evidence did NOT establish a dead token — a gateway denial 403s identically on every Figma URL, so the 'it 403s on both the copy and the library, therefore it is the token' control test was not valid. The conclusion happened to be right; the reasoning was not. Probe reachability before diagnosing a credential

resolvedThisSession: The 'can an agent draw into our Figma library' question is answered yes, with a worked example and a written recipe (figma/COMPONENT-DRAWING-RECIPE.md)
#252 filed: Figma Light/Dark identical across 189 variables. Distinct from #245 (that is the code-side CSS emission bug); both say dark mode is the least-verified surface in the system
#253 filed: variant-grid ordering decision, with the Button evidence, defaulting 2026-10-05

Three Figma mechanics recorded so they are not rediscovered: a component set does not grow to fit its variants (resize BEFORE repositioning or the outer row/column is silently clipped); defaultVariant is positional, not child order; fills[0].color returns the BAKED colour so it cannot prove a binding is live — resolve valuesByMode through its alias chain instead
Confirmed the staging copy is a faithful duplicate: 50 pages, 339 variables across 3 collections. The Figma MCP reporting only a 'Cover' page is lazy page loading, not an empty file
Storybook SSO blocker retired as stale — verified off via the Vercel project API, not assumed
Explained the CANCELED Vercel deployments: the Ignored Build Step restricts builds to main by design, not a fault

Root-caused why every REST-dependent Figma gate was dark: api.figma.com was blocked by the cloud environment's network policy, not (only) by a bad token. The Figma MCP was never affected because it routes via Anthropic's MCP proxy — which is why the StatusDot drawing pilot worked while the gates stayed dark

Root-caused the pnpm install 403: 'Host not in allowlist: registry.npmjs.org', and established that registry.npmjs.org bypasses the agent proxy via noProxy, so it needs the default-package-managers option rather than a Custom entry
